title: fix(scripts): scanSource's @returns declares the interpolation array it returns
body:
Fixes #9424

`tsconfig.scripts.json` compiles `scripts/**` with `allowJs: true` and `checkJs: false`
on purpose (objectui#3494), so a `.ts` consumer's type for `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs`
is inferred from the `.mjs` source steered by JSDoc — **the docblock IS the type**.

`scanSource`'s `@returns` named two properties while the function returns three
(`return { comment, literal, interpolation };`), so the declared return was narrower
than the real one and `scanSource(src).interpolation` was a compile error on a property
that genuinely exists and is genuinely populated — the delimiter-reachability flag array
whose post-processing keeps `check-entry-guard.mjs`'s statement slicer in sync.

## Premise re-derived on this branch's base, not taken from the card

Base `7098eed365`. The card anchored to `fb4ec65daf` and named `:220` / `:436`; both
re-derived here and both still correct at that base — `@returns` at **:220**, the
three-property `return` at **:436**. After the edit the docblock grows by four lines, so
the same two anchors read **:220** and **:440**.

## Acceptance: a diagnostic flip measured with the compiler, both legs in the same run

The card counted **0** `.ts` files in the program reading `.interpolation` today, so
"something red went green" was never available. The instrument is `ts.createProgram` +
semantic diagnostics under the real `tsconfig.scripts.json` options (parsed by `tsc`
itself), against the pre and post trees.

| snippet | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `scanSource(s).interpolation` | `TS2339: Property 'interpolation' does not exist on type` | **no diagnostic** |
| `const { comment, literal, interpolation } = scanSource(s)` | `TS2339` | **no diagnostic** |
| `scanSource(s).nosuchProperty` | `TS2339` | **`TS2339` — STAYS an error** |
| `const { alsoNotThere } = scanSource(s)` | `TS2339` | **`TS2339` — STAYS an error** |
| `scanSource(s).comment` *(control, known direction)* | clean | clean |
| `scanSource(s).literal` *(control, known direction)* | clean | clean |

The third and fourth rows are the load-bearing ones. "Reading `.interpolation` is clean"
is also satisfied by a return type destroyed into `any` or given an index signature, where
*every* name reads clean — so each widening case is paired with a genuinely-absent
property that must stay `TS2339`. It does, and its message now enumerates all three real
properties (before: two).

Subject confirmed **in** the program before trusting any green:
`tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json --listFiles` lists 936 files, line 571 is
`scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs`; an impossible sibling path is absent (0), and the
objectui#9324 pin test is present as a positive control.

## The function body is byte-identical

objectui#9424 is a defect in the docblock, not in the scanner. sha256 of the declaration
through its own closing brace, no trailing newline:

```
before  8e715c3a20dc63fc     (lines 222-437)
after   8e715c3a20dc63fc     (lines 226-441, same bytes)
guard   e3b0c44298fc1c14     = sha256 of the empty string, i.e. what "hashed nothing"
                               would have printed — it did not
```

## The `@typedef` question: measured, and deliberately NOT taken

The card asks — without ruling — whether the three arrays deserve a named `@typedef`,
since call sites destructure the shape. The triage comment rules it out of scope. The
measurement agrees with the triage, so the narrow fix stands.

Population: every direct `scanSource(` call in the **code** of all **4,947** tracked
JS/TS-family files at base `7098eed365`, comments stripped by the module's own
`stripComments` so a mention in prose is not scored as a call.

| how the result is consumed | sites |
|:--|--:|
| destructured at the call site | 18 |
| a single member read at the site | 10 |
| **whole result bound to a name** | **0** |
| unclassified (1 declaration + 2 string literals inside fixtures/error text) | 3 |
| *hand-written named types duplicating the shape* | **0** |

A named typedef earns its keep when something needs to **name** the shape — a variable
annotation, a parameter type, a return type elsewhere, or a duplicated hand-written type
to deduplicate. Measured: none of the four exist; every consumer destructures or reads one
member at the call site, where inference already supplies the type without a name. A
typedef would add a second declaration site with no reader — the same class of drift this
change exists to close. Matcher controls: an impossible type name scored 0, the same
matcher shape on a name that certainly exists scored 309.

## Reverse verification (ablation), both legs proven on disk

Fix committed first, then the `@returns` reverted to its pre-fix two-property form.

- Mutation proven on disk, not by the editor's exit code: pre-fix text count `0 → 1`,
  post-fix text count `1 → 0`, blob hash moved `fefd9819… → 561d2857…`.
- Body hash stayed `8e715c3a20dc63fc` — the ablation touched only the docblock.
- **New pin test: 3 failed / 5 passed.** The three that went red are exactly the two
  widening cases plus the "message enumerates all three" case. The five that stayed green
  are `.comment`, `.literal`, both absent-property cases and the in-program check — so the
  file did not fail wholesale.
- **objectui#9324's pin test under the same mutation: 10/10 green.** Its subject is
  `@param`, not `@returns` — that is what shows the red above is my tag being
  load-bearing rather than `allowJs` or the harness.
- Restore proven by state, not by exit code: blob hash back to `fefd9819…`, `git diff HEAD`
  zero lines, post-fix text count back to 1. Pin test green again, 8/8.

## Why this is a separate card and not a rider on objectui#9324

objectui#9324's dispatch named `scanSource` as **the control that was already correct** —
what proved the missing `@param` on the other three was a missing tag rather than `allowJs`
failing to type anything. Editing the control inside PR objectui#9423 would have dissolved
its own proof, so it left `scanSource` byte-identical. Different defect class, same file.
⛔ Not to be folded back retroactively. Nothing about objectui#9324 is undone here.
